reason: Strumate = bearing a struma, a swelling on one side at the base of a moss capsule. This follows the earlier rule for 'strumose', which maps to FLOPO gibbous (swollen on one side).

'Almost frond-like' describes a moss stem system branched in one plane like a fern frond. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has frondiform, so there is no value to approximate, and two statements do not justify a new term.
'Sub-' marks an approximate value. Isodiametric maps to PATO isometrical, as in config/flora_union_pairs.tsv.
A fragment of a moss stem cross-section description ('superficial cortical cells ...'). It names a layer of the stem, not a quality.
Unclear what a 'tail' is on a whole plant: a growth form with no standard botanical meaning, and the examples give no context.
Not a botanical word. Probably an OCR or transcription error.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A comparative wall thickness without the cells it is compared with, as already decided for 'thinner-walled'.

label: tristichous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inserted in three vertical rows along the axis that bears it.
reason: Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a tristichous term (only PATO_0001952 distichous). This standard leaf-arrangement term, used for sedges and mosses, is a sibling of distichous and of spirally arranged (FLOPO:0991114).

target: new: two attributes that both hold: triangular (PATO_0001875) and discoid (PATO_0001874)
reason: Moss brood bodies that are flat discs with a triangular outline. Both values hold at once, as decided for 'silvery-hyaline'.
Sphagnum hyaline cells with one pore each: a count of pores. 'Porose' alone maps to PATO porous, but that would lose the count, which is the diagnostic fact.
Leaf cells that bulge on both sides of the lamina are convex on both surfaces. 'Weakly' is a degree word and needs no term.

target: docs/odp/12-part-of-qualified-whole.md: hairy PATO_0000454 on the bearer; white PATO_0000323 (approximate) on trichome PO_0000282 part of the bearer
reason: The colour belongs to the hairs, not to the calyptra, as decided for 'whitish-hairy' and 'covered with white hairs'.
Says a part (membrane gaps in the walls of Sphagnum hyaline cells) is present, but neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for it, and the bearer 'hyaline cells' has no class either.
Hyaline leaf cells with (faint) fibrils are fibrillose, which is PATO fibrillary (synonym fibrillate). 'Traces of' is a degree word.
Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for the bearer (protonematal flap). Also, 'distinct' qualifies the point, so a plain negation of mucronulate (FLOPO:0991055) would misstate it.
States that a part is absent, but the pad of cells on the costa has no PO or FLOPO class, as already decided for 'without an adaxial pad of cells'.
Moss endostome cilia without lateral appendages. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has an appendiculate term, and 'appendage' was rejected as a generic part, so nothing can be negated.

Says an orchid lip callus is absent. 'Callus' was rejected as a generic part (config/flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv), and PO plant callus (PO_0005052) is tissue-culture callus, not this structure. The bearer 'lip limb' has no class either.

target: limbidium (no PO or FLOPO class yet; a FLOPO anatomy class part of leaf margin PO_0020128 is needed) absent
reason: Says a moss leaf border of differentiated cells is absent, matching the presence rule for 'limbidiate'. The rule needs the limbidium part class first. Until then the proposed 'elimbate' class covers the same meaning.
A calyptra that is not split up one side is the mitrate rather than the cucullate kind. The statement is the negation of PATO split.

Pseudostomata of Sphagnum capsules are not true stomata, so PO stomatal complex (PO_0002000) would be wrong, and neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for them. Also, the example puts them on the pseudopodium, which looks like a parsing slip.

target: new: two attributes that both hold: yellow (FLOPO:0988004) and transparent (PATO_0000964)
reason: A clear, yellow-tinged cell: a colour and a transparency that hold together, as decided for 'silvery-hyaline'. Hyaline is a synonym of PATO transparent.

label: seriate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of plant structures by virtue of their being arranged in one or more distinct rows or series.
reason: No term says 'in rows' without a count. This would be the parent of uniseriate, biseriate and multiseriate (FLOPO:0991090, 0991089, 0991084). When a count is given, the count pattern applies instead.
A part, not a quality, and 'basal lobe' was rejected as a generic part. The trunk example is a French fragment about something else.
Two statements with apparently different senses: a flat leaflet outline and a hollow petal (calceolate). Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a term, and the evidence is too thin for a new one.

target: cystolith (no PO class; a FLOPO anatomy class under or part of idioblast PO_0000283 is needed) present
reason: Says a part is present, as decided for 'cystoliths' and 'cystolith-bearing'. The rule needs the cystolith part class first.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (colour darker than the leaf lamina surface)
reason: A comparison that names its second term (the surrounding leaf surface), so it goes through the relation-to-another-part pattern. It is not rejected like a bare 'darker'.

label: bistratose
definition: A stratified quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being two cell layers thick.
reason: Same meaning as 'bistratose', proposed in an earlier batch with this parent and definition. Merge as a synonym of that proposal, not as a separate class.

target: new: two attributes that both hold: elongated (PATO_0001154) and clavate (PATO_0001883)
